result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had pain in your right knee. You had a knee replacement many years ago. The pain and soreness slowly got worse.

An X-ray showed the plastic part (the poly) of your knee replacement was very worn.

You had an operation called a poly exchange. The doctors changed the plastic parts of your right knee replacement.

You recovered well. You walked with a little help in physical therapy. Your oral pain medicines worked well. The anesthesia team removed your nerve block.

Your condition when you left was stable. Your INR was 1.9 when you left. The INR is a blood test.

You are going home with your son. He will help you and look after you.

## What you need to do
1. Go home to the care of your son.
2. Eat your regular diet.
3. Put weight on your right leg as you can manage (as tolerated).
4. Keep doing your physical therapy exercises.
5. Have lab checks twice a week. These are for your INR while you take Coumadin.
6. See Dr. ABC in two weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- Follow-up with Dr. ABC: in two weeks.
- Coumadin: 4 mg a day.
- Vicodin 5/500 mg: one to two tablets by mouth every 4 to 6 hours.
- Home medicines: the letter says to resume them. It does not name them.

The letter does not say who arranges the lab checks. It does not say how long you will take Coumadin or Vicodin. It does not give the exact date of the follow-up visit.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Who will arrange my twice weekly lab checks?
- How long will I take Coumadin and Vicodin?
- Which home medicines should I take again?
- What is the date of my visit with Dr. ABC?

## When to get urgent help
Call the office or go back to the emergency room if you have any of these:
- more redness
- more swelling
- drainage
- fever
- any worry about the operation or the cut (incision) site

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
